# vep-rs 0.3.2

vep-rs 0.3.2 is a performance release with no change in output: on every gated input the annotation is byte-identical to 0.3.1, and the whole of each batch is now annotated, filtered, rendered and freed in one pass over the worker pool, with bgzip input inflated through libdeflate. Measured against 0.3.1 under the same whole-genome protocol (the median of 20 machines per chromosome at 16 threads, summed over the chromosomes), the whole of gnomAD v4.1 falls from 974 to 724 s on ARM Graviton4 and from 1,219 to 1,169 s on x86, and the whole of gnomAD v2.1.1 from 586 to 282 s and from 835 to 476 s, with peak memory at most 2.4 GB on any chromosome; the two smallest datasets, 1000 Genomes Phase 3 and high-coverage, are 24 to 35 percent faster on ARM and within 2 percent of 0.3.1 on x86. The default thread count now stops at 32 logical CPUs, where the wall time stops improving; anyone running on hosts wider than 32 vCPUs with the default `--fork` should upgrade.

## Upgrade notes

- `--fork 0`, the default, uses every logical CPU up to 32 instead of every logical CPU. A host with more than 32 logical CPUs annotates faster under the new default; an explicit `--fork N` behaves as before and is never capped.
- Flags, input formats, output formats and the JSON cache format are unchanged; a cache converted for 0.3.0 is valid.
